mechanism: Enumerate random FX rate equations from Market Watch 6-letter pairs; balance and normalize multi-leg synthetic positions equivalent to a target instrument; score each polygon by SwapFactor = SwapPlus/SwapMinus (direct vs reverse side structure) using lot coefficients LotK chained by bid and contract size. The best SwapFactor maps a cross-pair funding/carry cost surface usable as a sensor of which synthetic hedges pay vs cost overnight.
data_needed: SYMBOL_SWAP_LONG/SHORT (points or percent modes), SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_VALUE/SIZE, contract size, bid for conversion to deposit currency, Market Watch FX pairs.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: FX majors/crosses composed of EUR,USD,JPY,GBP,CHF,CAD,NZD,AUD,CNY,SGD,NOK,SEK; overnight swap charging Mon–Thu (triple Wed–Thu); no intrabar TF—hold-as-long-as-possible horizon.
why_new_for_mis: Turns broker swap tables into a searchable multi-leg synthetic carry/funding sensor rather than single-pair swap lookup—MIS can rank funding regimes across polygons.
quote: If the accrued positive swap of the existing circuit is greater than the negative modulus, then such a circuit is considered profitable.

mechanism: For a fixed entry rule, iterate expiration minutes and take-profit distances on history; keep only digital measurements of the three preceding candles (length pips, body pips, color R/G) whose profitable cases never share an expiration with a losing case; store matching color-aligned ranges (e.g. R(22-31)-(2-26);G 13-3;G 21-11) as a live match filter before the base system may fire.
data_needed: Broker-specific M1 OHLC from ≥2009 (5-digit era); per-candle length/body/color in pips; exhaustive backtest over expirations and TP distances; periodic DB refresh.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M1 primary; method claimed for any market with long history; TP 5–15 pips best covered; larger distances sparse.
why_new_for_mis: A history-conditioned sequence sensor: only candle-triplet microstructures that never co-occurred with losses at a given hold horizon pass—finer than generic pattern catalogs.
quote: It is assumed that the probability of the occurrence and repetition of a successful deal increases if the combination of its digital measures is repeated in the trading history with no losing cases.

mechanism: From combination-scalping statistics, author observes coordinating deviation/correction sizes in pips: 37.5, 75, 112.5, 150, 187.5, 225. EURUSD typically corrects within 37.5 (rarely 75+); 225 pips is a standard one-way daily target unit (2–3 units common). Daily/weekly unit = 37.5×60 = 2250 pips (=10× M1 units). Use these as discrete intraday range/volatility rulers.
data_needed: Intraday EURUSD (and dependent pairs) pip excursions from arbitrary open points; M1 and D1/W1 scales.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD as foundation; other FX pairs more nervous; M1 primary, also daily/weekly.
why_new_for_mis: Discrete harmonic pip ladder as a FX volatility/range sensor tied to EURUSD leadership—usable as session range regime bins.
quote: For EURUSD, this deviation usually does not exceed 37.5 pips. Rarely it reaches 75 pips and more.

mechanism: Universal Bernoulli-fractal recursion for price (or equity) inside a symmetric corridor: average steps S = K^2 when corridor width scales by K relative to a known corridor; average lifetime T = T0·K^2. Validated for integer and float K via nested corridor limits. Enables estimating mean time-to-touch for wide corridors from short-corridor statistics when history lacks enough wide-corridor crossings.
data_needed: Empirical mean lifetime T0 inside a known-width corridor P0; target corridor width P; optional Monte-Carlo/fractal container (Upper/Lower MidS and SummProbability).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic pricing/trading corridors; random-walk case p=0.5 in this part; applicable where history is short for large corridors.
why_new_for_mis: Closed-form mean-reversion-time / corridor-dwell sensor that extrapolates beyond sparse large-barrier statistics—useful when MIS lacks long history for wide bands.
quote: if we know, let's say, the average lifetime of a price inside a symmetric channel, we can calculate the average lifetime of a price inside any other channel.

mechanism: Generalize average steps to Ss[m,n,p]=(n^Pn[p])*(m^Pm[p]) with power prototypes for step-up bias p≠0.5; solve for P[U]=(2pS−S+m)/(n+m) and conditional step counts S[U,u], S[U,d], S[D,u], S[D,d]. Outputs probability of first hitting upper vs lower bound and expected path composition—a directional regime sensor for price inside an asymmetric band.
data_needed: n,m step counts to upper/lower borders; p = Prob(step up); fitted K≈0.582897, A≈2.189246 for power prototypes; optional fractal simulation table for calibration.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Abstract price/trading corridors; any instrument once barriers expressed in equal steps; MathCad/MT5 validation tables.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a calibrated hit-probability and dwell decomposition for asymmetric barriers under biased steps—stronger than symmetric random-walk barrier formulas alone.

mechanism: Per bar, CopyTicksRange(COPY_TICKS_INFO) between bar open times; average (ask−bid) over ticks to ActSpread; compare to DeclaredSpread=spread[]*_Point. Normalize levels to EURUSD-equivalent 5-point stdPoint from instrument average price so spreads across pairs are comparable.
data_needed: MT5 tick database (bid/ask flags); bar times; SYMBOL_POINT; optional EURUSD for standardization.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, USDMXN, GBPAUD, GBPJPY, USDJPY, GBPUSD, EURGBP; M1 (~500 bars), M5 (~200), M30+ (~100); weekend and after 20:30 UK highlighted.
why_new_for_mis: Operational liquidity sensor: true mean tick spread vs broker-declared, cross-symbol standardized—feeds cost-of-immediacy and broker quality into MIS.
quote: the actual average spreads, the red line, versus the brokers documented spread, (black dashed line) are mostly twice as large as the declared spread

mechanism: Same ActSpread series shows regime shifts: ~2× declared in normal hours; ~3× (~15 points on EURUSD) on news/volatility; 4–10× after 20:30 UK and over weekends. Treat clock/session and event windows as liquidity regimes for tradability gating.
data_needed: ActSpread time series; session clock (UK/server); optional news calendar alignment.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M1 and M30 examples; majors USD-attached preferred (USDCAD,USDCHF,USDJPY,EURUSD,GBPUSD).
why_new_for_mis: Explicit time-of-day/event liquidity-regime labels from measured spreads, not from volume alone.
quote: Don't even consider trading after 20:30 UK time (21:30 on chart server time), it could well be 4, 5, 6 times or even much higher

mechanism: Generalize Bernoulli to N states via fractal tuples: count unique trade characteristics (profit buckets, lifetime, volume, etc.) that form a complete group; compute state probabilities and multi-nomial combination masses A[h]·∏p[s]^i[s]. Cluster historical deals into finite state sets for filtering or reweighting strategy samples.
data_needed: Deal sample with profit, open/close time (lifetime), optional volume; finite unique-value state dictionary; Pow(N,n) completeness check.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Backtests/signals equity-reducible strategies; example 7-order toy table; n=30 steps illustrated for 2- and 3-state systems.
why_new_for_mis: Turns trade/backtest history into an explicit multi-state probability sensor and clustering filter—usable as a strategy-regime or outcome-mix fingerprint.
quote: Sample clustering can serve as a good filter to enhance trading performance of existing systems.

mechanism: From multi-outcome deal series build B[i], TL[i]; choose corridor ~⅓ of min peak-to-trough move so both borders are hit; measure empirical P*[U], T*[U], T*[D]; search two-state step params (p, n=m, Pr, T[u], T[d]) matching those via Part-III math model; slope-correct KT so MP/MT matches final B/TL. Compresses any equity curve to four sensors: p, Pr, T[u], T[d].
data_needed: Per-deal profit and lifetime; balance and cumulative-time arrays; corridor MinD; math-model P[U], S[·,·].
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Five synthetic random strategies; method claimed strategy- and market-agnostic once deal PnL/time exist.
why_new_for_mis: Compresses complex multi-state PnL paths into a two-state dwell/hit sensor set simulable without the original market—MIS can fingerprint strategy curves compactly.
quote: As a result, we get a set of four values which completely describe our strategy — instead of huge arrays that describe more than two states

mechanism: Envelopes = MA ± fixed % of MA. In trends, require price to cross the outer envelope (not merely the MA) before treating a MA cross as valid—filters whipsaw/false breakouts. Uptrend: buy when price > upper band, exit when price < lower; downtrend mirrored; sideways: fade touches of opposite bands.
data_needed: iEnvelopes(period, MA method, applied price, deviation %); close vs upper/lower buffers.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Chart _Symbol/_Period; examples period 14, deviation 0.10–0.15; any TF user chooses.
why_new_for_mis: Operationalizes band distance from MA as a trend-vs-sideways / false-breakout regime gate rather than raw MA cross.
quote: the price crossed the Moving Average upwards but did not cross the upper band of Envelopes indicator. So, we cannot take action according to this crossover only
